audits.resolution_reason: Role-color distractor separates authority from a color-blind rival but is rejected by the declared validator. Intended-domain decision needed; not a reproduced generated-label defect.
audits.text:
## c1ee27b39d13

**Suspected shortcut/domain question: top-border color 4 is never separated
from “any nonzero top cell.”**

The unedited seed `0`, sample index `0`, difficulty `medium` replay passes the
generator validator. Adding one top-border color-3 distractor at `(0,1)` leaves
the selected Racket authority well-defined: it ignores the distractor and uses
only color-4 columns. A rival that selects every nonzero top-border cell adds an
extra column and differs from the authority.

The counterfactual is intentionally rejected by current `self_check` (“top
selector row may contain only 0/4”), so this is not a reproduced generated-label
defect. It is a domain/teaching question: within every documented generated
scene, the fixed-color role and the color-blind shortcut are observationally
identical. A maintainer should decide whether non-4 border distractors belong in
the intended training domain.

Evidence: `checks/audit/c1ee27b39d13/case.json` (case SHA-256
`38de3938bc379bc23dbc27c564c742a07619ccddd41fac25947da0a8178fac92`),
with supported authority transcript at
`checks/audit/c1ee27b39d13/racket.json`. Generator SHA-256 is
`27632d96e3daa1f7fa723d231a41c912c80b840305667f05bcee89d32baf5ec6`;
rule hash is `6a46c5a9b416`. No patch was made because this is audit-only.
